card.name: Comma or 'and' before 'including' or 'many of'
card.fires_on: A comma (sometimes 'and' or 'in') right after a plural or general noun phrase, where the next words are likely 'including...', 'many of which', or 'some of them'. Seen in adverse-event reports and in general descriptive prose.

modes.label: Event report then 'including'
modes.description: Comma after a named adverse event, leading into 'including fatal cases'.
modes.example: There have been postmarketing reports of acute pancreatitis<<,>> including fatal pancreatitis, in patients treated

modes.label: List then 'many of which'
modes.description: Comma after a counted or listed group in general prose, leading into 'many of which' or 'some of whom'.
modes.example: Pandora alone plays the music of more than 100,000 artists<<,>> 70 percent of whom are independent

modes.label: Linking word before 'some'
modes.description: 'and' or 'in' after a clause about many cases, leading into 'some' of them.
modes.example: Many of these events were serious<< and>> some resulted in death.

card.writes: It promotes quantifier words like 'many' and 'some', so the text goes on to say how many or which of the group.
card.plain: It marks the spot after a group of things where the text is about to say 'many of them' or 'some of them'.
